lines: As winter approaches, so does recruitment season.
Winter hits the Tertnikiva province pretty hard, which means an increase in volunteer recruits for the People's Government Armed Forces.
However, leading economists say that this may be connected to an increase in crime nationwide.

In his article, economist and Partine Westnorthern University graduate Jonas Lasochka postulates that Tertnikiva's constant export of young, working-class men and women to Our Armed Forces has irreparably damaged their mining industry.
Financially, they may stay afloat because of Our Lady's purchase of swaths of land for army training.
However, fewer miners means an increase in imported coal, and not many can afford those high prices through the winter.
Today, Jonas Lasochka joins us to talk about how this could affect the recovery effort.
